A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASCIIEval/ASCIITune research despite the changed title and substantial revision. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, human recognition results, supervised fine-tuning experiments and analyses by artwork size and category.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds rationale-assisted training, resolution and fine-tuning experiments, and character-perturbation and font tests.

M1.justification: Beyond v1's direct answer-supervised fine-tuning, v2 introduces GPT-5-generated rationales, answer-based filtering and training on rationale-plus-answer outputs. It also introduces low-resolution inference and selective LoRA adaptation of vision versus language components (Sections 5.2 and 6.2; Appendix H). These change training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: The recognition task and reported coverage remain 3,526 ASCIIEval examples across 359 concepts and 11,836 ASCIITune examples. Appendices J–K add limited scenarios involving corrupted characters and alternative fonts. TableEval, SGP-Bench, OCRBench and TextVQA contribute existing leaderboard scores to correlation analyses, rather than newly reported task runs.

E2.justification: The evaluated model set expands substantially, adding GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-pro, Claude-opus-4, DeepSeek-V3, newer Qwen/Gemma/Llama models and InternVL3, while removing Chameleon. The training comparisons introduce thinking and component-specific adaptation controls. Models included in size/category comparisons also change; these are not simply renamed or relocated comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 replaces the earlier Llama/Llava modality-mixing training experiments with Qwen-based comparisons using filtered rationale data and different training schedules. New protocols include resolution sweeps and perturbing 100 cases initially solved in all three modes. Pass-rate reporting disappears, and an oracle based on success with either individual modality is added. Macro/micro accuracy and the artwork-size bins are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds cross-benchmark correlations, generational comparisons, rationale/thinking controls, resolution and component-training ablations, data-quality checks, and font/corruption sensitivity tests. It removes v1's MLLM-versus-backbone comparison, modality-mixing SFT ablation and per-model correctness annotations in the retained case examples. Size and category analyses persist with updated model selections.

E5.justification: v2 introduces Pearson correlation estimation across overlapping models and benchmark leaderboards (Sections 5.1 and 6.1; Appendix G). Neither version reports model-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The three 100-example human evaluations are retained without an increased repetition count.

E6.justification: Extensive new results include GPT-5's 55.90% text and 87.81% image accuracy and Qwen3-8B's 35.66% rationale-assisted result versus its 28.28% baseline. Robustness and intervention results are added, while earlier Chameleon, backbone and SFT entries disappear. GPT-4o's text/image/combined scores change from 42.88/82.68/76.52% to 43.40/82.62/75.41%, but its specified checkpoint also changes, preventing a same-setting performance interpretation.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains equivalent text-only, image-only and combined-input prediction mappings, with renamed variables and separately numbered equations. Neither version contains substantive theoretical results or proofs; the new oracle comparison is an empirical evaluation device.

C1.justification: The benchmark and modality-fusion concerns remain, but v2 adds central claims about generational regression in open-source MLLMs, an OCR–holistic-vision trade-off, and improvement through rationale training and low-resolution prompting. The earlier contribution concerning multimodal training's failure to improve backbone LLM perception is removed from the principal findings.

C2.justification: v2 adds an OCR-specialization explanation for recognition failures and attributes rationale-training benefits to decomposition while identifying tokenization as a possible spatial bottleneck. It newly discusses training-data noise, annotation ambiguity, hallucinated rationale fragments and font sensitivity. These substantially extend the original size/category and modality-fusion interpretations.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds filtering counts, rationale verification, learning rate and full-parameter/LoRA schedules; other appendices add token-length and rendering-font information. Conversely, v1's greedy/temperature-zero decoding, output-token limits and deployment details disappear. Appendix A changes release wording to future tense. Reproducibility remains limited by inconsistent Qwen2.5-VL size labels: 8B in Table 2 versus 7B in the leaderboard.

R1.justification: v2 substantially extends positioning through comparisons with TableEval, SGP-Bench, OCRBench and TextVQA, arguing that ASCIIEval isolates visual perception and exposes tension with OCR. Related work adds these benchmarks, FrontierMath, Multi-IF, MMStar and newer model literature while removing several earlier general-benchmark references. Publication-status updates to retained works are not counted as additions.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and related-work discussion are extensively revised. The unified results section becomes separate LLM, MLLM and modality-synergy sections. ASCIITune construction and category analyses move into appendices, which are reorganized and expanded. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The opening examples and distribution chart are reorganized into a benchmark overview. Leaderboards are redesigned, including a consolidated appendix table and scaling/generation panels. New displays cover correlations, tokenization, rationales, oracle comparisons, perturbations and fonts. Earlier comparison tables disappear, and retained case figures lose their model-correctness panels.

improvement.justification: The new component-training controls, corruption/font tests and explicit data-quality limitations make the benchmark more diagnostically useful. However, lost decoding details weaken reproducibility, and important conclusions exceed the evidence: OCR correlations do not establish the asserted causal trade-off, while Section 7's universal degradation claim conflicts with Table 5—for example, Qwen2.5-VL-7B scores 37.01% with combined inputs versus 34.83% with images alone. These problems limit the net quality gain despite the substantial expansion.
